title: Sterility of first crosses differs from sterility of hybrids

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Sterility of first crosses differs from sterility of hybrids

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: The sterility of first crosses between pure species, whose reproductive organs are perfect, is a different phenomenon from the sterility of their hybrids, whose reproductive organs are functionally impotent.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: On the Origin of Species by Means of Natural Selection, or the Preservation of Favoured Races in the Struggle for Life

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: Pure species have of course their organs of reproduction in a perfect condition, yet when intercrossed they produce either few or no offspring. Hybrids, on the other hand, have their reproductive organs functionally impotent

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci Origin of Species claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Charles Darwin, On the Origin of Species (1st ed., London: John Murray, 1859), Chapter VIII, “Hybridism”; section “Distinction between the sterility of first crosses and of hybrids”. Scope: plants and animals crossed between species

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on darwin1859-ch08-01: resolvable-now, resolvability 0.74

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The two outcomes are standard, separately measured reproductive-isolation components. Existing experimental datasets resolve the distinction even though no comprehensive cross-taxon database exists.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Separate fertilization or F1-production success from fertility of surviving F1 hybrids and compare their physiological causes. Distinct failure stages and mechanisms support the claimed distinction.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value: Crossing records are dispersed and taxonomically biased.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
data adequacy: 0.58
analysis feasibility: 0.7
operationalizability: 0.92
data existence: 0.72
discriminating power: 0.8

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: One public compilation already splits barriers into components that match the two phenomena for many fly pairs, and that split can be reanalyzed quickly. The physiological claim is broader than Drosophila, and plant or vertebrate crosses with a recorded stage of failure are not in a comparable open table. Where the stage is scored directly, the contrast is informative rather than confounded.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: For species pairs, separate failure to produce offspring when parental gametogenesis is normal from sterility of F1 hybrids whose own gametogenesis fails. A systematic difference in the stage of failure supports two phenomena; a single shared stage of reproductive collapse would count against the distinction.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Outside Drosophila, crossing tables that record the stage of failure are scattered in papers.

Plants and non-fly animals in the stated scope are poorly represented in the open compilation.

The distinction is close to a definition by stage, so some of the result is built into the scoring.

data adequacy: 0.48
